:::{#exm-not-matrix-induced-norm}
#### A symmetric matrix that induces no norm

The [symmetric matrix](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix) $\matr{B} = \diag(1, -1)$ is not [positive definite](#def-positive-definite),
so it has no [matrix-induced norm](#def-matrix-induced-norm).
The [square root](algebra-basics.qmd#def-square-root) $\sqrt{\qform{\matr{B}}{\vx}}$ is undefined at $\vx = (0, 1)$:

$$
\ba
\qform{\matr{B}}{\vx}
&= 1 \cd 0^2 + (-1) \cd 1^2
&& \text{(expand the quadratic form)}
\\
&= -1,
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

and $-1$ has no square root in $\reals$.

<!-- no-figure: the example is one quadratic-form value at one vector -->

:::
